[Gray_Sloth gave me permission to post their thoughts over here, because I felt they were really poignant.]

"Oh the circular reasoning of mental illness we meet again. You want to kill yourself because you are depressed, and we know you are depressed because you want to kill yourself. The question I ask is, am I wrong though? You can call it depression if you want, but is my supposed depression incorrect?

If you go to a movie and find that you don't personally like it and try to walk out early, nobody says you are sick and puts you in a straight jacket before you can leave.

So at what point did we decide that the question "Do you like life" has a correct answer and it is not "no"? This is a wildly authoritarian and insecure attitude to have, if we truly believe that life is so great why do we have to forcibly coerce people into staying?

The idea that being suicidal is inherently indicative of mental illness rests on the notion that wanting to live is the correct state of mental health, that satisfaction with life is healthy and dissatisfaction is unhealthy. When did opinions become pathological?

If I don't enjoy watching football does that also mean I am sick? Should I have to take drugs and be forced to watch football until I do like it?

It should be obvious to everyone that mental illness is the ultimate ad hominem for those who commit the thought crime of suicidality, because at that point nothing they want matters they are just depressed."

I think it would be good if users can add a reason for why they deleted their comment. This will hopefully stop users from wondering why the comment was deleted.

It can also be added for moderators, so there can be more transparency.

I'm wondering if it should be mandatory (for both users & moderators).

I think it could be also used for threads. Like, when a user deletes a thread, there should be an anonymous comment stating the reason for the deletion.

Option to add reason why you deleted a comment.

Great idea. I'd like to go a step further and add "deleted by user" or "deleted by mod/admin" when comments are modded. Doesn't have to be those words, just some way to know if it was a self delete or not would be awesome.

I think people should be free to delete their comments without having to explain why they did it. It is their comment after all. If they really wanted to explain why they deleted a comment, they could just edit the comment, and replace it with an explanation for the deletion. It you made this mandatory, that's basically forcibly taking a freedom from users, and I don't think I can support that. Also what's the benefit? Just so people with curious minds can get an explanation? I don't think that's a strong enough reason to justify taking away people's right to remove themselves from a thread, for whatever reason they please.

That being said, I think it is a good idea to distinguish deletions made by mods and deletions made by users. It is also a good idea to require mods to explain their reason for deletions.

Deletions by mod are already distinguished as "deleted by a moderator". Deletions by user are shown as "deleted by author".

Implementing a reason for deletion requires quite a bit of effort on both backend and frontend and I don't think this is a priority at this point.

If users want to give a reason why they removed a comment, they can edit it.

Reason mechanism would also interfere with account deletions, leaving a note like "user deleted his account and chose to remove all comments".

It is an interesting idea, but our current focus is on what we can do to make WhoaVerse more user friendly and easier to use as well as what we can do to help our userbase grow. Please keep the ideas coming! :)
